intervals.note: Season wording only ("1999--2000 austral summer"); the interval is stored at January 2000 with the season in `display`.
intervals.quote: The telescope was deployed at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole research station during the 1999--2000 austral summer and conducted observations of the CMB throughout the following austral winter.

end.note: last season reported in the 2004 three-year paper

intervals.label: observations
intervals.note: First observations were made through the 2000 austral winter; polarization observations followed in 2001-2003 (abstract of astro-ph/0409357: data "throughout the 2003 season"). No source consulted states when DASI stopped observing; 2003 is the last season it reports.
intervals.quote: The telescope was deployed at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole research station during the 1999--2000 austral summer and conducted observations of the CMB throughout the following austral winter.

intervals.label: observations ended
intervals.note: Inferred terminal event: the 2004 paper analyses "the complete 3-year data set"; no fetched source states an end-of-observations or decommissioning date.
intervals.quote: We present the analysis of the complete 3-year data set obtained with the Degree Angular Scale Interferometer (DASI) polarization experiment

placements.note: MAPO stands about 200 m from the Dark Sector Laboratory (BICEP1 characterization paper); shares the Dark Sector site record because no separate coordinates are published.
placements.quote: The telescope is situated atop the inner of two concentric towers attached to the Martin A. Pomerantz Observatory (MAPO), 0.7 km from the geographic South Pole.

sensor_count.quote: DASI is a 13-element, co-planar interferometric array operating in ten 1-GHz bands spanning 26 − 36 GHz.

summary.plain: A 13-element microwave interferometer on a tower beside a South Pole observatory that, in 2002, made the first detection of the polarization of the Big Bang afterglow.
summary.technical: 13-element, co-planar interferometric array operating in ten 1-GHz bands spanning 26-36 GHz, on the inner of two towers attached to MAPO; temperature anisotropy 140 < l < 900 (2000) and polarization (2001-2003).
